intro: Buying in downtown Knoxville is different from buying in the suburbs. Condo fees, parking, building rules and historic guidelines all matter. Our Downtown office is on Gay Street, so we know the buildings and the blocks around them.

We also help buyers across Knox County and the counties next to it. Whether you want a loft near Market Square, a porch in Fourth & Gill or a yard in Fountain City, a Wallace Downtown agent will guide you from the first showing to the keys.
buyers.why_lead: The reasons buyers tell us they chose Knoxville and Knox County.
why: Market Square, the Old City, Gay Street, the riverfront and World's Fair Park are all close together and easy to walk.
The University of Tennessee, UT Medical Center and many local employers keep Knoxville busy and growing.
Tennessee does not tax wages, which helps many buyers stretch their budget.
The Urban Wilderness, Ijams Nature Center, the Tennessee River and the Smoky Mountains are all within reach.
Lofts, condos, historic homes, new subdivisions and land, all inside one county.
I-40, I-75 and I-640 meet here, and McGhee Tyson Airport is about 20 to 25 minutes from downtown.

buyers.inspect: We schedule inspections and, for condos, review the HOA budget, rules and reserve fund. For older in-town homes, we help you check wiring, plumbing, foundations and any historic district rules.
faq: What should I check before buying a downtown condo?
Look at the HOA fee and what it covers, the reserve fund, any special assessments, parking, pet and rental rules, and recent sales in the building. We gather all of it for you.
Are there historic district rules?
Some Knoxville neighborhoods, like Fourth & Gill and Old North Knoxville, are historic overlay districts. Exterior changes may need approval. We tell you if a home is in one before you make an offer.
Do I pay city and county taxes?
Homes inside Knoxville city limits pay both city and Knox County property taxes. Homes outside the city pay county taxes only.
How much do I need for a down payment?
It depends on the loan. Some loans allow as little as 3 to 3.5 percent down, and some condo buildings have lender rules. We connect you with local lenders who know downtown buildings.
How are schools assigned?
Knox County Schools assigns schools by address. We confirm the zoned schools for every home.
Can I buy from out of town?
Yes. We do live video tours, send local notes on each home and handle inspections and closing with e-signatures.
How fast do homes sell?
It changes by area and price. Well-priced homes near downtown can sell quickly, so we set up instant alerts and help you be ready to write an offer.
Do you work outside downtown?
Yes. We help buyers across Knox County and the counties next to it, including Anderson, Blount, Loudon, Roane, Sevier, Jefferson, Grainger and Union.

intro: Selling a home in downtown Knoxville takes local know-how. Buyers compare condo fees, parking, views and walkability, and they compare your home to the other units in your building. Our Downtown office is on Gay Street, so we know what buyers are looking for.

We also sell homes across Knox County and the counties next to it. A Wallace Downtown agent will price your home from real local sales, market it everywhere buyers look and stay with you to the closing table.
who: People who work downtown, at UT or at the medical centers and want to walk to work, dinner and events.
Buyers moving from bigger, more expensive cities who want Knoxville's lower costs and easy lifestyle.
Empty nesters trading a big yard for a condo, and investors looking for rentals near UT and downtown.
sellers.features: condos with parking, river views, historic homes and walkable locations
sellers.drone: downtown, the river and your neighborhood
faq: How do you price a downtown condo?
We compare recent sales in your building and nearby buildings, then adjust for floor, view, parking, size and HOA fee. We do not rely on online estimates.
Should I fix things before I list?
Some small fixes pay off, like paint, lighting and cleaning. We walk through your home and tell you which projects are worth it and which are not.
How long will it take to sell?
It depends on price, location and condition. We share the latest days-on-market numbers for your area when we meet.
What do I need from my HOA?
Buyers will ask for the HOA rules, budget, recent meeting minutes and any planned assessments. We help you gather them early so the sale does not stall.
Do you use professional photos?
Yes. Every listing gets professional photography, and many get video, drone and 3D tours.
Where will my home be advertised?
On the MLS, Zillow, Realtor.com, wallacetn.com, social media and email to our buyer list, plus the Wallace network of agents across East Tennessee.
What does it cost to sell?
Common costs include the commission, title fees, and any repairs or credits you agree to. We give you a net sheet so you know what you will walk away with.
Can you help me buy my next home too?
Yes. We can help you time your sale and purchase, whether you are moving across Knox County or out of state.
